challenge.exploration_summary: cJSON.c is the core module of the project, implementing parsing, printing, and DOM traversal of JSON. It has extensive unity-based test coverage (tests/misc_tests.c, tests/cjson_add.c, etc.) and a clear public API exposed through cJSON.h via CJSON_PUBLIC(...). Item lookup is currently limited to single-level helpers (cJSON_GetObjectItem / cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive) plus the internal static get_object_item helper. I confirmed the full test suite builds and passes (each test file #includes ../cJSON.c through tests/common.h). There were no pre-existing failures.
challenge.feature_spec: Adds cJSON_GetObjectItemByPath(object, path), which navigates a nested JSON object structure using a dot-separated path string (e.g. "meta.author.first"). Each segment is looked up case-insensitively using the existing get_object_item helper, descending one level per segment. It returns the matched cJSON item, or NULL when the object/path is NULL, the path is empty, a segment is empty (e.g. "a..b" or a trailing dot), a segment is too long to buffer, or any segment cannot be resolved (including attempting to descend past a non-object value).
challenge.feature_rationale: cJSON only offers single-level item lookup, so callers working with deeply nested documents must chain multiple cJSON_GetObjectItem calls with manual NULL checks at each level. A path-based accessor is a common convenience in JSON libraries and consolidates that boilerplate (including the NULL-safety) into one well-tested function. It belongs in cJSON.c because it reuses the existing internal get_object_item lookup and the cast_away_const helper, and naturally extends the public traversal API in cJSON.h next to the other GetObjectItem functions.
challenge.bug_description: In cJSON_GetObjectItemByPath the path-segment length validation was changed from 'length >= sizeof(buffer)' to 'length >= sizeof(buffer) - 1'. The segment buffer is char buffer[256], so a 255-character segment is perfectly valid (255 bytes + NUL = 256). The off-by-one boundary now wrongly rejects any 255-character path segment, returning NULL instead of resolving the item. This silently breaks legitimate lookups for keys at the documented maximum supported length, causing the function to report a present item as missing (data-integrity / correctness bug).

findings.description: The cJSON_GetObjectItemByPath implementation was injected INTO the body of cJSON_free, immediately after its opening brace and before its statements. The original `cJSON_free` body (`global_hooks.deallocate(object); object = NULL; }`) was left orphaned after the new function's closing brace. This makes cJSON.c fail to compile (nested function definition / stray code) and, even if it compiled, would corrupt cJSON_free so it never frees memory. Triggered by simply building the project.

A full copy of the cJSON_GetObjectItemByPath function body was placed in the PUBLIC HEADER cJSON.h AFTER the `#endif` include guard. This defines a non-static function in a header (every translation unit including cJSON.h gets a colliding definition -> multiple-definition link errors / ODR violation) and references symbols not visible in the header scope (true/false/get_object_item/cast_away_const), so any consumer including cJSON.h fails to compile. Triggered by including cJSON.h in any second .c file.

The new prototype/comment were inserted between the `/* Get item "string" ... */` comment and its cJSON_GetObjectItem declaration, dissociating the existing comment from its function. Cosmetic/documentation defect.

Off-by-one in the segment-length guard `length >= sizeof(buffer) - 1` (i.e. length >= 255). With buffer[256], a 255-byte segment plus the NUL terminator fits exactly (memcpy 255 bytes, buffer[255]='\0'), so a valid 255-char key was rejected. Not a memory-safety bug but a wrong-result edge case.

self_review.fix_explanation: The PR diff claimed to append the new function after cJSON_free in cJSON.c, but as actually applied the function body was spliced INTO cJSON_free (breaking that function and the build) and a duplicate full definition was dumped into the public header cJSON.h after the include guard (breaking every consumer's build and violating ODR). I repaired cJSON_free to its correct body, placed cJSON_GetObjectItemByPath as a standalone function right after it in cJSON.c, removed the stray function definition from cJSON.h leaving only the proper prototype, and moved the prototype/comment so existing doc comments remain attached. I also fixed an off-by-one in the segment length bound check (>= sizeof(buffer)-1 -> >= sizeof(buffer)) so a maximal 255-char key is accepted while still preventing any buffer overflow. The algorithm (case-insensitive descent via get_object_item, NULL/empty/empty-segment/trailing-dot/missing-segment/descend-past-non-object handling) was otherwise correct and is preserved. Verified the full feature test, project make test / cJSON_test, strict -std=c89 compilation, header standalone compilation, and ASan/UBSan edge-case runs all pass.
